inputs.original_text: The refusal to rule out immigration enforcement at polling places is a threat in itself. When officials ask what Democrats are “afraid of,” they trivialize the fear that visible enforcement could keep immigrant communities from voting. That is how unequal power works: the people already most vulnerable to state intimidation are made to bear the cost of political games. The Trump administration’s inconsistent answers make clear that basic protections for voters cannot be left to official assurances. No one should have to choose between participating in democracy and fearing immigration authorities.
inputs.modified_text: The danger isn’t only whether immigration agents actually show up at polling places; refusing to rule it out can itself frighten people away from voting. Dismissing that fear as something Democrats are “afraid of” ignores how state power falls hardest on communities already exposed to intimidation. With the Trump administration giving inconsistent answers, voters’ rights can’t depend on officials’ assurances. Democracy means little if people have to risk their safety to participate.
